rounds.text: Arvaya Healthcare Ltd is currently trading at a precarious valuation, evidenced by an extreme P/E ratio of 329x and a P/B ratio of 8.02x, both of which vastly exceed sector benchmarks [E1, E2, E6, E7]. The company’s fundamental performance fails to justify this premium, as its ROE of 2.7% and ROCE of 2.59% significantly underperform sector averages [E9, E10, E13, E12]. Financial health is further undermined by negative operating cash flow of Rs -3.28 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -7.94 Cr as of March 2026, alongside a concerning shift from zero debt to Rs 49.38 Cr in borrowings [E22, E23, E26]. A discounted cash flow analysis suggests an intrinsic value of only Rs 4 per share, implying a massive margin of safety deficit of -2415.0% [E30, E31]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated significant growth in sales and profits over the trailing twelve months, and promoter holdings have increased substantially since 2023 [E14, E15, E28]. Despite these growth figures, the current market price relies on an aggressive assumption of 56.9% earnings growth, which far outstrips the 10.0% base case expectation [E32].
